newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian blue chips lead GDRs higher.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian blue chips lead GDRs higher.

text.p: Indian blue chips led London's global depositary receipt (GDR) market higher, outperforming the local market rally but easing into the end of the trading day, while a rare issue from the Baltics saw strong demand.
"The blue chips did well -- they outpaced the local market rally," said one trader, citing Bajaj, Reliance, SBI and IPCL.
The Cazenove Indian GDR Index rose 0.50 points, or 0.75 percent, to 67.32 after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index gained 13.86 points to 2,997.88.
But the trader said the local rally was largely driven by speculative and domestic purchasers.

"The spurts of activity we've been seeing show that the market is ready for a more broad-based rally if some fundamentally good news comes in," added Paribas salesman Tony Singh. "Better liquidity will mean a firmer rally mid-year."
Market players are hoping for lower interest rates and good news ahead of the February budget.

Reliance GDRs were bid at 11.00, after closing on Tuesday at 11-1/4. SBI ended down five ticks at 15-3/8, and Bajaj at 30.00, after 30-3/4 yesterday. IPCL was off a fraction at 10-1/4 after 10-1/2 at Tuesday's close.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 0.59 points, or 97 percent, at 60.92 points, with the premium over the local market at 19.01 percent compared with 20.85 percent yesterday.
However Taiwanese and Korean GDRs firmed.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 3.36 points, or 5.79 percent higher at 61.40, a premium of 48.67 percent over the local market.
And Capel's Taiwan GDR Index ended 0.45 points, or 0.48 percent firmer at 93.77, a premium of 3.14 percent over the local market.
Among new issue news, Nomura International said a $6 million GDR isssue for Lithuanian dairy company Birzai Milk Company was heavily oversubscribed.
"The $6 million issue...was five times oversubscribed as the new share-capital was registered in Lithuania today," Nomura International said in a statement.
"This represents the first time a non-bank corporate from the Baltic region has tapped the international equity markets through a GDR issue," it added.
Nomura and co-lead Bilniaus Bankas recorded demand from more than 40 institutional accounts after a week-long roadshow.
